name: Process: Design the ninety-day calibration loop back to the packet
text_content:
P41, and finding 18.6. The record says universal problems are design problems (WP p.17) and never says what a hire that does not hold is, where its post-mortem goes, or what in the hiring system is fixed when it happens. Without the loop, a failed hire is fixed at the person and the interview that produced it runs unchanged. Row 71. Routes to Session 14 for where a hire that does not hold is read.

Filed by Session 6 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmhnt. Reasoning lives on the S6 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

comment.text: Session 14 added the loop's second trigger. A horizon window opened inside a person's first year runs the calibration read again on that packet at the leads' review, in order: the seat sheet's horizon against the rows the window's form read not yet, the practical's rows and scoring anchors, the fourth-read baseline and the supplied lines, the anchor set for the reads that mattered, and only then the interviewer note; writing to the calibration record and to versioned changes on the sheet, the rows, the kit, the fourth read's questions, or the interviewer's training record, never to any page about the person, and counting first-year windows per seat class per period to the reset as the hiring system's first leading indicator. This closes Session 6's finding 18.6 as a mechanism. S14 page, section 7; P29; work items A15 and A23.
